data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"If the panel and the checklist make identical judgments on all evaluation items, then the panel exhibits no genuine reliability beyond mere compliance; within a single evaluation, evidence of reliability requires the panel to diverge from the checklist in a direction that tracks the objectively correct outcome.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the checklist is perfectly accurate on the evaluation items, divergence is unnecessary and identity does not indicate mere compliance.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the panel diverges from the checklist but not systematically toward correctness, divergence indicates noise, not reliability.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the checklist is nondeterministic or has slack, identity may not hold even under mere compliance.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Mere compliance produces judgments that are a deterministic function of the checklist. If the panel's judgments are identical to the checklist's, the panel has added no information. Genuine reliability requires the panel to add information beyond the checklist, detectable as systematic divergence toward correctness on items where the checklist errs.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
